edits.new: Requirements follow each meaning's own wording and necessary implications, not customary cases. For each required parent condition absent from the child's wording, check recognized ordinary variants that change that condition while preserving the child's defining kind or activity and every stated restriction. Test the property actually required, rather than only a different method or feature. A familiar kind name does not by itself impose every descriptor in the parent's definition, and a variant's name alone does not establish admission. Conditions neither required nor necessarily implied may vary; their absence alone is not ambiguity. Illustrations inherit their alternative's defining conditions and do not import a separate node's whole scope. General knowledge may clarify language but must not select a convenient scope; materially different supported readings that change coverage leave the affected judgment unresolved.
